cue_frames.expected_caption: Responder is the personal workspace for a named member.
Check the account and department, then read My Status and My Staffing on Home.
People, Units, and Calls provide the wider operating picture.
A community response team can use the same pattern to show who is available and
which incident each person is joining.
Every name and incident shown here belongs to our fictional training department.
First launch introduces Resgrid
Responder, Instant Notifications,
and Interact with Calls.
Use Next to read each page, Skip to leave the introduction,
or Let’s
Get Started on the final page.
Language is available on the login screen.
These introduction pages describe intended features; they do not establish that this
browser has received a push notification or exercised a native device permission.
Use Change Server URL before signing in when your organization
supplies a different API endpoint.
The Server selector offers regional choices and Custom; Server URL takes
the API origin without slash api slash v four or a trailing slash.
This recording uses only the local fictional API.
Return to Username and Password, then Login using your own authorized account.
Keep credentials outside screenshots and shared recordings.
Login with SSO opens a separate entry screen with Username or Email and
Department ID, which is optional.
Continue starts the organization’s configured identity flow.
The training environment has no usable identity-provider discovery
configuration, so this is an entry-screen walkthrough only.
A deployed organization must verify its provider, return link, and any additional
challenge on the intended platform before relying on that sign-in path.
Recover your account explains that a recovery code is entered after a
password or organization sign-in.
Without that code, contact the department administrator or support; this screen
cannot turn off two-factor authentication.
Back to sign in returns to the normal entry point.
We are showing the actual no-challenge view, without changing credentials,
creating recovery codes, or claiming that verification has completed.
On Home, select Status and read the offered choices before
changing your personal state.
This department offers Responding, Not Responding, On Scene, and Standing By.
Its labels and transitions come from department configuration.
The example selects Responding and opens Set Status: Responding.
After the completed action, My Status shows the saved state and destination.
Use the displayed result to confirm the change.
The destination step separates Calls, Stations, and POI.
Select the intended destination
before moving to Add Note.
In this exercise, the community medical standby is the chosen call and the note
clearly says it is an Academy exercise.
Save completes the personal status change, and
the Home
card displays that destination.
Read any required-field instruction in your department rather than assuming
every status uses the same steps.
Staffing records your availability for assignment.
This department offers Available, Delayed, Unavailable, Committed, and On Shift.
The example chooses Available, uses Add Note to state the training
availability window, and checks
Review and Confirm before Submit.
My Staffing then shows the saved result.
Personal status and staffing serve different coordination needs, so read
both cards when handing over a community care or search-team duty period.
People shows the member’s group, role, status, staffing, and update time.
Search personnel
and Filter Personnel narrow that picture by Groups and Roles.
Units has its own search and opens resource
details such as
Location and Vehicle Information.
These are useful reference views for a search-and-rescue team, security
patrol, or industrial standby.
Reading a unit here does not establish an active shared-device crew session.
Open Sign-in and security
to review Authenticator app, Passkeys for
this app, and Recent verifications.
The actual training account says its authenticator is not set up,
has no app passkeys, and has no verifications in the last thirty days.
Those are configuration states, not proof of a successful challenge.
Setup or credential changes belong to the organization’s approved security
process and are outside this exercise.
Responder approvals lists device approval availability; this
account shows Approvals stopped.
A configured approval request must be matched to a sign-in you initiated,
including its number, before any approval.
No challenge or hardware notification was exercised here.
For a shared or handed-over device, Logout asks for
confirmation
before clearing local session data.
The declared web recording adapter preserves the source confirmation
text and buttons; native confirmation remains platform-specific.
